title: LuaLander
description: Easy questions from the first game: landing, fuel, coins, events and particles.

questions.context: This runs every moment you hold a thrust key. The tank starts full at fuelAmountMax = 10.
questions.prompt: With a full tank, about how long can you keep thrusting?
questions.hint: Time.deltaTime turns "per frame" into "per second". So the tank loses 1 per second - and it holds 10.
questions.explanation: Each second costs 1 fuel, and a full tank is 10, so about 10 seconds of thrust. Without Time.deltaTime it would drain 1 per frame and be empty in a blink.

questions.context: This runs when the lander touches a landing pad. It checks how fast you came in.
questions.prompt: You touch the pad at speed 5. What happens?
questions.hint: Compare the two numbers: your speed (5) and softLandingVelocityMagnitude (4). Is 5 bigger?
options: Crash - game over, you landed too hard
Successful landing with a speed bonus
questions.explanation: 5 > 4, so the if is true and the game ends with TooFastLanding. To land safely you must touch down at speed 4 or less.

questions.context: This also runs on landing. Vector2.up points straight up; transform.up is where the top of the lander points. Their dot product is 1 when the lander is perfectly upright and gets smaller the more it tilts.
questions.prompt: You land tilted far onto one side. What does this code decide?
questions.hint: Tilted far means dotVector is much smaller than 1. Is that below 0.90?
questions.explanation: A big tilt pushes dotVector well under 0.90, so the if is true: TooSteepAngle, game over. You have to land nearly upright.

questions.context: This runs whenever the lander bumps into anything. Only landing pads have a LandingPad component.
questions.prompt: You fly into a rock. What happens?
questions.hint: The ! means NOT. Read the first line as: "if the thing I hit does NOT have a LandingPad..."
questions.explanation: A rock has no LandingPad, so TryGetComponent returns false, ! makes it true, and the lander crashes. TryGetComponent checks for a component and fetches it in one call.

questions.context: This runs when the lander flies through a fuel canister. The tank holds at most fuelAmountMax = 10.
questions.prompt: You have 8 fuel and grab a canister. How much fuel do you have now?
questions.hint: 8 + 10 = 18. Now look at the if: what happens when fuel is more than the maximum?
questions.explanation: 8 + 10 = 18, but the if caps it at fuelAmountMax, so the tank is simply full: 10.

questions.context: GameManager.cs listens for the lander's OnCoinPickup event. This method runs every time you collect a coin.
questions.prompt: You collect one coin. What happens to your score?
questions.hint: Look at the number inside AddScore( ).
questions.explanation: Every coin calls AddScore(500). The lander only announces "I picked up a coin"; GameManager decides what a coin is worth.

questions.context: This is the top of Lander.cs. GameManager, the UI and the audio scripts all need to talk to the one lander in the scene.
questions.prompt: How do the other scripts find the lander?
questions.hint: Instance = this stores the lander in a static property. Static means you reach it through the class name: Lander.____
options: Each one creates its own new Lander
They search the whole scene every frame
The lander finds them and calls them
questions.explanation: This is the singleton pattern: in Awake the lander stores itself in the static Instance, and any script can then write Lander.Instance - e.g. GameManager does Lander.Instance.OnLanded += ...

questions.context: This is LanderVisuals.cs - the script that owns the thruster flames. Lander.cs only fires the event OnUpForce when you thrust; it never touches particles.
questions.prompt: Who turns the flames on when you thrust?
questions.hint: += means "when this event fires, call my method". Which script contains that line?
options: LanderVisuals - it listens to OnUpForce and switches the particles on
Lander.cs, right after it adds the force
questions.explanation: LanderVisuals subscribes to OnUpForce and reacts by enabling the particles. Logic (Lander) and visuals (LanderVisuals) stay separate - the same split FerryHeist uses.

questions.context: When you let go of thrust, LanderVisuals switches emission off. The flame does not vanish at once - it fades out.
questions.prompt: Why does the flame fade instead of disappearing instantly?
questions.hint: Emission is the part of a particle system that spawns new particles. What about the particles that already exist?
options: Emission off only stops NEW particles - the ones already flying live out their lifetime
The particle system is slowly destroyed
The lander keeps thrusting for a moment
questions.explanation: Turning emission off stops spawning; particles already alive finish their lifetime. That is why the flame fades naturally - no extra animation needed.

questions.context: GameManager.cs keeps the level number here. Every new level reloads the whole scene, which creates a fresh GameManager object.
questions.prompt: You finish level 1 and the scene reloads. How does the game still know you are on level 2?
questions.hint: Compare levelNumber with score on the last line. Which word does score not have?
options: levelNumber is static - it belongs to the class, not to the object that gets reloaded
Unity saves it to a file
It doesn't - you always restart at level 1
questions.explanation: Static fields belong to the class, so they survive the scene reload. score is not static, so it starts again at 0 each level, while levelNumber and totalScore carry over.
